blocks.text: # Git Made Code Collaborative. Proofpress Makes Intelligence Compound.
Most documents are snapshots of the final state of thought.

We can read what an essay, strategy, research memo, or proposal eventually became. We usually cannot see which evidence shaped it, what changed along the way, why it changed, which alternatives were rejected, or what remains uncertain.
The artifact survives. The reasoning required to understand and continue it often does not.
That was already a weakness in human knowledge work. Multiplayer AI turns it into infrastructure debt.

Humans and agents now work on the same artifacts across chats, models, tools, teams, and organizations. Each session learns something the file alone cannot express: why a sentence changed, why one direction won, what a reviewer challenged, and which constraint the next collaborator must preserve.
But the file moves while that decision trail stays behind. The next person or agent receives the output without the history that made it trustworthy.
## More AI output does not necessarily mean more knowledge
AI is making the production of text, analysis, and decisions expand at machine speed. But trust, shared context, and institutional memory still move at human speed.

This is the deeper problem behind AI slop. It is not only that some generated content is generic or wrong. It is that an output can have no stable origin, no checkable account of how it changed, and no safe way for another actor to inherit it.
An output without provenance can spread. It cannot reliably compound.

If every session leaves behind only a polished final answer, adding more agents creates more conclusions that cite, summarize, and rewrite one another without trustworthy lineage. The organization accumulates words while repeatedly losing the knowledge required to evaluate and extend them.
Intelligence that cannot be safely inherited cannot compound. Intelligence that cannot compound cannot become collective.
## Record the decision, not the private conversation
The answer is not to preserve every prompt, every message, or an agent’s private chain of thought.
Most of that material is noisy, sensitive, or irrelevant to the next collaborator. Replaying a conversation also does not tell us which parts were ultimately accepted into the shared work.

What deserves to persist is the external, checkable trail admitted into the artifact: accepted edits, evidence, consequential decisions and rejections, attribution, verification results, and explicit gaps where provenance remains unknown.
This is not a transcript of cognition. It is the durable account of what entered the work.
The goal is not to preserve the conversation. It is to preserve what the conversation caused the work to become.
## Git’s deeper lesson
Git’s greatest contribution was not merely that it stored versions of code.

Git gave software a durable shared history: common state, lineage, attribution, branching, comparison, and a way to continue work without sharing the same room or remembering the same conversation. That history helped make code globally collaborative.
Knowledge work now needs an analogous trust layer.
This does not mean turning every document into a repository. A line diff cannot express the decision behind a strategy, the evidence behind a claim, or the reason an alternative was rejected.
The lesson to carry forward is larger than Git’s interface or storage model:
> **Git made code collaborative. Proofpress makes intelligence compound.**
## A shared, checkable past

Proofpress is the trust layer for multiplayer AI: an open, agent-native ledger
that travels with the artifact.

Proofpress turns accepted changes, decisions, and evidence into an artifact-native ledger that can remain attached to the work as it passes between humans, agents, sessions, and tools. The artifact—not any single chat product or collaboration destination—becomes the common surface.

LLM wikis and repository knowledge tools solve a different problem: they synthesize what a codebase or repository knows now. But knowledge artifacts do not stay inside one repository or one destination. They move across chats, tools, teams, and organizations. When the artifact moves, its decision lineage should move with it. Git history is repository-native. Proofpress provenance is artifact-native.
A normal document tells you what it says now. A durable knowledge artifact should also help answer:

1. **What do we know?**
2. **Why do we believe it?**
3. **Who can continue thinking from here?**

When the relevant history travels with the artifact, a later human or agent does not have to start from zero or blindly trust the latest file. It can inspect what changed, distinguish computed facts from attributed testimony, see what was rejected, find missing provenance, and continue from the correct base.

This is a trust layer, not a promise that every statement is true, every identity is proven, or every event was captured. Its job is to keep the boundaries between captured, checked, attributed, and unknown visible—so silent context loss cannot masquerade as shared knowledge.
If Proofpress succeeds, it will not be another docs product.
It will be an open protocol for humans and machines thinking together: a way to turn one-off output into knowledge that can be checked, inherited, challenged, and extended.
It will give every human and agent that touches the work a shared, checkable past.
It will make the history of the work as durable as the work itself.
And it will let intelligence compound without requiring trust to be diluted at the same rate.
> **Scale intelligence. Preserve trust.**
